record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Which hyperboloidal initial data arise from spacetimes with smooth conformal null infinity, and what class of Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York conformal data (gamma_ab, A_cd, tau) constructs such hyperboloidal initial data?

evidence.quote: Characterise those hyperboloidal initial data arising from a spacetime with a smooth conformal null infinity. Describe a class of LCBY data (Yab• A,cd, 't) which can be used to construct such hyperboloidal initial data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider the vacuum Einstein equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold (M, g). A hyperboloidal initial data set is a triple (S, h, K) where S is a 3-manifold with boundary ∂S, h is a Riemannian metric on the interior, and K is a symmetric 2-tensor playing the role of the second fundamental form, such that S embeds into (M, g) as a spacelike hypersurface whose boundary ∂S lies on (a cross-section of) future null infinity ℐ⁺ and which is asymptotically null near ∂S. A spacetime (M, g) is said to admit a smooth conformal null infinity if there exists a conformal compactification (M̃, g̃ = Ω² g) with smooth boundary ℐ on which Ω = 0, dΩ ≠ 0, and g̃ extends smoothly to ℐ.

The Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York (LCBY) conformal method parametrizes solutions of the Einstein constraint equations on S by the following free conformal data:
• a Riemannian metric γ_ab on S (conformal class representative),
• a symmetric, transverse, traceless tensor A_cd with respect to γ (the TT-part of the rescaled extrinsic curvature), and
• a scalar function τ on S (the mean curvature).
Given (γ_ab, A_cd, τ), one solves the Lichnerowicz equation for a conformal factor φ and the vector momentum constraint for a vector field W, and then recovers physical data (h, K) on S by appropriate conformal rescaling.

Problem. 
(a) Characterise intrinsically those hyperboloidal initial data sets (S, h, K) that arise as the induced data on a spacelike hyperboloidal hypersurface of a vacuum spacetime (M, g) admitting a smooth conformal null infinity ℐ⁺.
(b) Identify and describe explicitly a class of LCBY conformal data (γ_ab, A_cd, τ) on S — including their regularity and asymptotic behaviour at ∂S — such that the LCBY procedure yields exactly hyperboloidal initial data of the type characterised in (a).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been actively studied with substantial partial results but no complete intrinsic characterisation. Andersson–Chruściel proved that generic hyperboloidal data lead to polyhomogeneous (not smooth) expansions at ℐ, with smoothness occurring only for a non-generic subclass; necessary conditions such as vanishing shear at the conformal boundary are known. Recent work (e.g., 2025 results on hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities) continues to refine the LCBY-conformal-method construction of smooth hyperboloidal data, but a full characterisation remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: On hyperboloidal Cauchy data for vacuum Einstein equations and obstructions to smoothness of Scri
status_evidence.snippet: Generic asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data sets admit polyhomogeneous expansions, with only a non-generic subclass being free of logarithmic singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Smoothness at ℐ is obstructed for generic LCBY-type hyperboloidal data, so a full characterisation remains open.

status_evidence.title: Hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent construction of hyperboloidal initial data avoiding logarithmic terms at the conformal boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent work continues to identify subclasses of LCBY data yielding smooth ℐ, indicating only partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Smoothness at Null Infinity and the Structure of Initial Data
status_evidence.snippet: Friedrich's analysis relates geometric conditions on Cauchy data at the conformal boundary to smoothness of ℐ.
status_evidence.claim: Necessary conditions are known but the intrinsic characterisation is incomplete.
